hypotheses.justification: The definition of `f.ker` does not require quasi-compactness; it is the largest ideal sheaf below the family of componentwise ring-map kernels (`Hom.ker` and `ofIdeals` in `IdealSheaf/Basic.lean`). Quasi-compactness is only used by `ker_apply` to identify those ideals with the componentwise kernels. Without it, `f.ker` still lies below that family, whose ideals are radical because the target section rings over the reduced source are reduced (`Ideal.isRadical_bot.comap`). Thus `f.ker.radical` also lies below the family, so maximality gives `f.ker.radical ≤ f.ker`; the reverse inclusion always holds. This proves the same statement without `[QuasiCompact f]`.
